S1.title: CMS-2454-IFC fact sheet, June 1, 2026
S1.locator: Full page re-read 2026-10-19 (both chunks): Who is Affected; What the Requirement Means; Key Provisions table.
S1.excerpt: States must generally implement no later than January 1, 2027; affected adults may use activities, half-time education, or monthly income ("$580 per month in 2026"); a notice of noncompliance allows "30 calendar days to demonstrate compliance or that the requirement does not apply"; disenrolled people "may reapply at any time".

S2.locator: Official PDF SUMMARY and DATES re-read 2026-10-19; preamble II.C.1 (Work) read through Federal Register full-text search excerpts of document 2026-11094. The 135-page rule was not read end-to-end.
S2.excerpt: Effective July 31, 2026; states must implement "no later than January 1, 2027". Preamble: "Many individuals work for themselves by being self-employed due to starting a business, owning a business, or as an independent contractor, and these activities meet the definition of work"; "an individual who performs duties as a property manager or building superintendent may receive compensation in the form of free or reduced rent ... the hours the individual spends performing these duties would count toward meeting the 80-hour requirement."

S3.title: Community Engagement Requirement IFC Overview, July 2026
S3.locator: All four retrieved chunks re-read 2026-10-19: Demonstrating Community Engagement (boxes A–F); Defining Qualifying Activities; Calculating Income and Minimum Wage; Mandatory Exceptions; Specified Excluded Individuals; Short-Term Hardship; Assessing Compliance.
S3.excerpt: States must use an individual’s MAGI-based monthly household income and the Federal minimum wage ($7.25 x 80 = $580); state or local minimum wages may not be used. Box F: seasonal-worker averaging; "A seasonal worker is described in section 45R(d)(5)(B)". At application the review period is "the 1, 2, or 3 consecutive months prior to the month of application, as specified by the State."

Noncompliance: "you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California".

summary.title: First choice: test the income route
summary.value: Countable unearned income can satisfy the monthly income route: currently $580, using MAGI-based household income.
summary.note: For rental and interest income, this is more directly supported than claiming trading hours. You still must satisfy all other Medi-Cal rules. No personal monthly amount was supplied.
summary.evidence: CMS slides: MAGI-based monthly household income; 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2): MAGI-based income for the MAGI-based household; AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6): MAGI-based financial methods; DHCS member letter: income from any source of at least $580 before taxes.

summary.title: Separate eligibility from engagement
summary.value: Most adult Medi-Cal financial eligibility extends up to 138% FPL; this is a separate test from community engagement.
summary.note: Income can satisfy the $580 floor yet exceed Medi-Cal’s upper limit. Do not treat all rent receipts, contract payouts, or account balances as MAGI.
summary.evidence: Covered California adult threshold; HealthCare.gov net income rules; CMS engagement income methodology.

summary.title: If income is below $580
summary.value: Recognized alternatives include 80 hours of qualifying work, community service, a work program, or a combination; at least half-time education is its own route.
summary.note: No earned wages are necessary for structured qualifying unpaid community service. The federal rule counts paid, in-kind and unpaid work, and its preamble names property managers paid in free or reduced rent and self-employed business owners. Acceptance of your own-rental management hours is not confirmed (F3); own-account Kalshi trading hours are not addressed by any official source reviewed (F2).
summary.evidence: CMS activity routes; 42 CFR 435.552(b) work definition; 91 FR 33348 preamble II.C.1 self-employment and property-manager examples.

summary.title: Check exclusions before counting hours
summary.value: Caregiving, pregnancy/postpartum, medical frailty, certain program participation and other exclusions may remove the activity requirement.
summary.note: No age, dependent, disability or other exclusion facts were supplied; none is assumed. Work-rule exclusions do not automatically excuse six-month renewals.
summary.evidence: Separate exclusions and renewal populations in CMS and DHCS materials.

summary.title: If Medi-Cal income is too high
summary.value: Covered California is the state Marketplace; financial help depends on eligibility and income.
summary.note: Zero wages alone is not the test. Losing Medi-Cal specifically for work-rule noncompliance is not a reliable route to subsidies: DHCS warns financial help is unavailable in that situation.
summary.evidence: Covered California program comparison and DHCS noncompliance warning.

summary.title: What California is doing
summary.value: DHCS describes automated information use, outreach, BenefitsCal document handling and resources for paid/volunteer work, training and education. The enacted statute (AB 2161) adds data-first verification and a duty to confirm conflicting data before adverse action. It also sets a 30-day period running from receipt of the notice and requires review of every other basis of eligibility before denial.
summary.note: No blanket exemption for zero earned income was established in the reviewed official materials; none of AB 2161’s listed exclusions, deemed-compliance categories or hardships is based on having no earned income. This guide cannot enroll you or guarantee zero paperwork.
summary.evidence: September outreach; corrected verification rule; AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2), (c), (f), (h), (i), (k), (n).

summary.title: Act on notices, not assumptions
summary.value: Federal deadline January 1, 2027; California statute: no sooner than January 1, 2027 and only after DHCS confirms its systems are ready; current DHCS page: work rules January 1, six-month checks March 1.
summary.note: A September outreach enclosure says both rules begin March 2027. Published discrepancy remains open on Flagged for Review; do not rely on a delay.
summary.evidence: Conflicting official dates reproduced in F1; AB 2161 §14005.69(d) and (q)(1).

sections.title: Work rules & timeline
sections.description: What changed, who is affected, and the routes that do not require wages.
sections.intro: Legal basis: Public Law 119-21 §§71119 and 71107; CMS-2454-IFC effective July 31, 2026. Read the correction with the original rule. This page is a relevant-provisions digest, not a claim to reproduce the entire law.

rows.title: Law and regulation
rows.value: July 4, 2025 law adds community engagement; CMS issued its implementing interim final rule June 1, published June 3, effective July 31, 2026.
rows.note: Implementation is generally required by January 1, 2027. California date inconsistency is flagged at F1.
rows.evidence: P.L. 119-21 table of contents (Secs. 71107, 71119); CMS fact sheet dated June 1, 2026; 91 FR 33348 DATES: effective July 31, 2026.

rows.title: Affected group
rows.value: Generally certain nonpregnant adults ages 19–64 in Medicaid adult expansion or relevant §1115 coverage, not every Medi-Cal enrollee.
rows.note: DHCS identifies the MAGI New Adult Group. U.S. citizenship by itself does not create a work-rule exemption. Age and actual aid category remain unknown.
rows.evidence: Who is Affected; ACWDL Policy and Excluded Populations.

rows.title: Income route
rows.value: Monthly MAGI-based household income at least 80 times federal minimum wage: $580 at $7.25/hour. Countable unearned income is included.
rows.note: Use federal—not California—minimum wage. The threshold can change if federal minimum wage changes. This is not the upper Medi-Cal income limit. California’s statute uses the same MAGI-based household test.
rows.evidence: CMS Calculating Income and Minimum Wage; 42 CFR 435.552(a)(6), (f)(2); AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6).

rows.title: Work-hour route
rows.value: At least 80 hours in a month; recognized work includes money-paid, in-kind and unpaid work. Self-employment is included in the federal discussion.
rows.note: The federal preamble gives a property manager or building superintendent paid in free or reduced rent as an example of in-kind work whose hours count, and says self-employment (owning a business) meets the definition of work. A job title or a full-time trading label alone does not verify qualifying duties or hours. F2 and F3 identify unresolved applications.
rows.evidence: 91 FR 33348 preamble II.C.1; CMS Defining Qualifying Activities; 42 CFR 435.552(b).

rows.title: Community service
rows.value: At least 80 hours of qualifying unpaid community service in a month can meet the requirement.
rows.note: Use a structured program under an established organization, for direct community benefit and not a partisan purpose. Recommendation: keep an organization-verified dated hours log; exact county document format is not established here.
rows.evidence: Defining Qualifying Activities: structured, nonpartisan community service.

rows.title: Education
rows.value: At least half-time enrollment in a qualifying educational program is a separate compliance route.
rows.note: School determines half-time status. Qualifying categories include specified higher education, career/technical, high-school and equivalency programs; not every online course qualifies. The member letter’s “part time” wording is flagged at F11.
rows.evidence: Defining Qualifying Activities; institution determines student status.

rows.title: Work programs and combinations
rows.value: 80 hours in qualifying work programs, or combined qualifying activity hours, can satisfy a month.
rows.note: Less-than-half-time education may combine with activities. CMS specifies credit hours × 3 × 4.33 for monthly hours in credit-hour programs; do not assume informal self-study counts.
rows.evidence: Defining Qualifying Activities; Combining Activities.

rows.title: Seasonal income
rows.value: Only a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B) may use a preceding-six-month average income at the federal threshold.
rows.note: AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(7), 42 CFR 435.552(g)(1) and DHCS’s public page (“Be a seasonal worker”) all require seasonal-worker status. The DHCS member letter’s broader “hours change frequently” wording is flagged at F7. Do not assume irregular Kalshi profits make you a seasonal worker.
rows.evidence: CMS box F; AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(7); 42 CFR 435.552(g)(1); 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B); DHCS Medi-Cal Changes; September outreach income bullet.

rows.title: Application look-back
rows.value: California statute: an applicant shows compliance for the one month immediately before the month of application.
rows.note: The federal rule lets states choose 1, 2 or 3 months; AB 2161 §14005.69(d)(1) and preliminary ACWDL 25-30 both use the immediately preceding month. When the rule starts for you remains open (F1).
rows.evidence: CMS What the Requirement Means; CMS Assessing Compliance Overview; ACWDL 25-30 Look-Back Month; AB 2161 §14005.69(d)(1).

rows.title: Existing-member renewal review
rows.value: Enrollees show one qualifying month between the most recent determination and the next scheduled redetermination (AB 2161 §14005.69(d)(2)); the September DHCS member notice says any month since last renewal.
rows.note: Preliminary December guidance assesses existing members at their next 2027 renewal. Do not assume monthly uploads or a six-month average for everyone. Actual notice controls case deadlines subject to law and appeal.
rows.evidence: Ways You Can Meet This Rule; Policy; AB 2161 §14005.69(d)(2).

rows.title: Six-month renewals
rows.value: Public Law §71107 changes adult expansion renewal frequency; current DHCS page says March 1, 2027 for six-month checks.
rows.note: Its exception list is narrower than the work-rule exclusion list: outside new adult group, pregnancy/postpartum, AI/AN, qualifying former foster youth. The member letter says six-month renewals begin “January 2027”. Date discrepancy F1 remains open.
rows.evidence: September letter background; March 2027 Six-Month Eligibility Checks.

rows.title: Verification and notice rights
rows.value: The state must use reliable available information before asking for more. A noncompliance notice gives 30 calendar days. In California the 30 days run from the date the notice is received (deemed 5 days after its date), and coverage continues meanwhile. Other bases of eligibility and a fair hearing must be offered before denial.
rows.note: Correction replaces §§435.557–435.558. From January 1, 2028 documentation is required when reasonably available, but no denial may rest solely on documentation that does not exist. Do not ignore a request because a data match might exist; no zero-paperwork guarantee.
rows.evidence: CMS What the Requirement Means; corrected §435.557(b)(2); AB 2161 §14005.69(k)(1)(B)–(E), (k)(2).

rows.title: Loss of coverage and reapplication
rows.value: DHCS warns work-rule noncompliance can end Medi-Cal and prevent Covered California financial help; reapplication for Medi-Cal is possible at any time.
rows.note: Notice includes appeal information. Losing coverage for excess income is distinct from losing it for failure of the work rule.
rows.evidence: You Could Lose Your Medi-Cal; CMS reapplication guidance.

rows.title: Other relevant change: past bills
rows.value: Current DHCS page says retroactive bill coverage is reduced starting January 1, 2027: one month for adults without children; two months for everyone else.
rows.note: This is a separate eligibility/coverage provision, not a way to meet community engagement; the Help Center still describes today’s three-month period. Specific case eligibility is not determined.
rows.evidence: Less Time to Get Help Paying Old Medical Bills; Help Center Retroactive Medi-Cal.

rows.title: California statute
rows.value: AB 2161 (Chapter 209, Statutes of 2026), approved September 14, 2026, amends Welfare and Institutions Code §14005.69 to implement the federal rule in Medi-Cal.
rows.note: It postdates preliminary ACWDL 25-30 and the August 31 member letter. It sets the look-back months, the MAGI-based income test, seasonal-only averaging, the 30-day period and other-basis review. It is implemented only after DHCS determines in writing that systems are programmed (§14005.69(q)(1)).
rows.evidence: AB 2161 chaptered text: digest, §14005.69(d), (e), (k), (n), (q).

sections.title: Income & eligibility
sections.description: Rental profit, savings interest, trading, and the distinction between assets and income.
sections.intro: Your income amounts, tax household, age, current coverage and county were not provided. All personal eligibility values remain blank on Flagged for Review. Do not characterize your total income as zero solely because earned income is zero.

rows.title: MAGI is not wages
rows.value: MAGI generally starts with adjusted gross income and adds untaxed foreign income, non-taxable Social Security and tax-exempt interest.
rows.note: Marketplace uses expected annual household income for savings. CMS engagement uses MAGI-based monthly household income; annual Marketplace figures cannot simply replace monthly review.
rows.evidence: MAGI formula; Marketplace annual estimate; CMS monthly income rules.

rows.title: Rental income
rows.value: Use net rental and royalty income; countable unearned income may meet the engagement income threshold.
rows.note: Do not use gross rent without allowed expense treatment. California’s statute and the federal regulation both use MAGI-based household income for the $580 test. Exact deductions, depreciation effects, losses and your resulting MAGI are not verified for your facts.
rows.evidence: HealthCare.gov net rental instruction; federal rule countable unearned income.

rows.title: Savings interest
rows.value: Interest and dividends, including tax-exempt interest, are included in the income guidance.
rows.note: Bank interest is different from the savings-account principal. The $580 route is not limited to wages; actual countable monthly amount is unknown.
rows.evidence: Investment income bullet; MAGI monthly income methodology.

rows.title: Trading income: general rule
rows.value: Capital gains count in the income guidance; taxable investment income is not excluded merely because it is not earned wages.
rows.note: Kalshi-specific tax classification, loss treatment and timing are not established; a targeted irs.gov search on 2026-10-19 found no event-contract or Kalshi guidance. Do not assume every contract is §1256 or that turnover/payout equals countable profit. See F2.
rows.evidence: Capital gains included; IRS topic is general securities guidance only.

rows.title: Trading tax status versus healthcare
rows.value: IRS general securities guidance says calling yourself a day trader does not establish trader status; securities trading gains are not subject to self-employment tax.
rows.note: This does not decide whether own-account Kalshi trading hours satisfy §435.552. No healthcare hours or tax classification is assigned from that IRS page.
rows.evidence: IRS Topic 429, Traders; separate federal healthcare work definition.

rows.title: Property manager versus landlord
rows.value: IRS says rental real estate income generally is not self-employment income; substantial services can change reporting.
rows.note: Managing property for clients versus managing your own rentals are different facts. No personal earned-income or work-hour determination can be made from the title “property manager.”
rows.evidence: IRS Publication 527; CMS work definition.

rows.title: Assets are a separate issue
rows.value: DHCS lists “No property limits” for MAGI Medi-Cal; non-MAGI programs require proof of property and have limits ($130,000 for one person through June 30, 2027; $21,000 from July 1, 2027).
rows.note: Owning rentals or savings is not itself a MAGI asset disqualification; income from them still matters. Non-MAGI alternatives require a separate review, not a blanket no-asset rule.
rows.evidence: DHCS Help Center Qualify Comparison; Medi-Cal Changes Asset Limits; income guidance.

rows.title: 2026 ceiling: one-person household
rows.value: 138% FPL: $22,025 annual reference; published monthly ceiling $1,836.
rows.note: Only a reference example—not an assumption that your household size is one. 2026 values are not a prediction of 2027 limits. Monthly/annual rounding differs.
rows.evidence: 2026 annual and monthly 138% columns; MAGI FPL effective January 1, 2026.

rows.title: 2026 annual reference: 3 people
rows.note: Reference only; both reviewed DHCS annual sources agree. Household composition and monthly income rules still apply. Sizes 2, 5, 7, 10 and 12 have conflicting annual figures; see F5.
rows.evidence: 138% annual column for this household size.

rows.title: 2026 annual reference: 4 people
rows.note: Reference only; both reviewed DHCS annual sources agree. Household composition and monthly income rules still apply. Sizes 2, 5, 7, 10 and 12 have conflicting annual figures; see F5.
rows.evidence: 138% annual column for this household size.

rows.title: 2026 annual reference: 6 people
rows.note: Reference only; both reviewed DHCS annual sources agree. Household composition and monthly income rules still apply. Sizes 2, 5, 7, 10 and 12 have conflicting annual figures; see F5.
rows.evidence: 138% annual column for this household size.

rows.title: 2026 annual reference: 8 people
rows.note: Reference only; both reviewed DHCS annual sources agree. Household composition and monthly income rules still apply. Sizes 2, 5, 7, 10 and 12 have conflicting annual figures; see F5.
rows.evidence: 138% annual column for this household size.

sections.title: Exclusions & exceptions
sections.description: Check these before choosing an activity route. None is assumed to apply to you.
sections.intro: Federal terminology distinguishes specified excluded individuals, mandatory exceptions (deemed compliance), optional short-term hardships, and state implementation exemptions. Public California materials often use “excused” or “exempt” more generally. This list summarizes the categories relevant to screening, not automatic approvals.

rows.title: Other eligibility groups / age
rows.value: Work rules do not generally apply to children, adults 65+, or people covered outside the applicable adult group.
rows.note: Other coverage groups have their own rules. Medicare is also addressed as a mandatory exception.
rows.evidence: CMS deck mandatory exceptions: "Under the age of 19"; Medicare Part A or Part B; other mandatory categorically needy groups. DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: rules do not apply to "Children (0–18)", "Adults 65 and older". ACWDL 25-30: Non-MAGI, Mandatory Children’s and Pregnancy groups excluded.

rows.title: Pregnancy / postpartum
rows.value: Pregnant individuals or those entitled to postpartum medical assistance are excluded.
rows.note: DHCS describes pregnancy and one year after. No personal pregnancy fact is assumed.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Pregnant or eligible for postpartum coverage in their state." DHCS: "Pregnant people (during pregnancy and one year after)". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(M).

rows.title: Child caregiver
rows.value: Parent, guardian, caretaker relative or qualifying family caregiver of a dependent child age 13 or younger is an exclusion category.
rows.note: 13 is included; CMS and the detailed DHCS changes page support 13 and younger. Exact family-caregiver relationship criteria still matter.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "dependent child 13 years of age and under". DHCS: "Parents and caregivers of children ages 0-13". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(E): "a dependent child 13 years of age or younger".

rows.title: Disability caregiver
rows.value: A qualifying caregiver of a disabled individual is an exclusion category.
rows.note: The federal rule has family-caregiver implementation criteria; not every informal helping relationship automatically qualifies.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "family caregivers of ... a disabled individual"; CMS deck family-caregiver criteria. AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(F) also lists the caregiver "of an individual with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation."

rows.title: Medical frailty / special needs
rows.value: Individuals medically frail or with special medical needs significantly impairing compliance are excluded.
rows.note: Serious physical/mental conditions and substance use may be relevant. Do not assume every diagnosis automatically meets the rule; county verification is needed.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: medically frail only if a condition "significantly impairs the individual’s ability to comply". DHCS member letter lists serious, complex or ongoing medical and serious mental health conditions. AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(H)(i)–(v).

rows.title: Veteran with total disability
rows.value: Veterans with a total disability rating are a specified excluded category.
rows.note: CMS slides specify 100% under 38 U.S.C. §1155. Veteran status alone is not enough.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: "total (100 percent) disability rating as defined under 38 U.S.C. §1155". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(G).

rows.title: American Indian / Alaska Native
rows.value: Specified American Indian / Alaska Native categories are excluded.
rows.note: The legal definitions govern, not a generic self-description. DHCS also lists this group among annual-renewal exceptions.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "American Indians and Alaska Natives". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(B)–(D): Indians, Urban Indians, California Indians, and people eligible for the Indian Health Service.

rows.title: Former foster care youth
rows.value: Qualifying former foster care children are an excluded category.
rows.note: DHCS describes under age 26 and in foster care on the 18th birthday. CMS identifies the statutory eligibility group.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: former foster care children described at section 1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(IX). DHCS: "People under age 26 who were in foster care on their 18th birthday". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(N): "Foster youth or former foster youth under 26 years of age."

rows.title: CalWORKs / TANF
rows.value: Already complying with TANF work requirements is an exclusion category.
rows.note: California outreach calls this meeting the CalWORKs work requirement; receipt alone is not stated as sufficient.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Meet the TANF work requirements". DHCS member letter: "Are meeting the CalWORKs work requirement." AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(I).

rows.title: CalFresh / SNAP
rows.value: Members of households receiving SNAP who are subject to SNAP work requirements are an excluded category under CMS guidance.
rows.note: Do not assume every CalFresh recipient qualifies: exemption from SNAP work requirements can affect this route.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: SNAP household members who "are not exempt from the SNAP work requirements". DHCS member letter: "Are receiving CalFresh and are not excused from the CalFresh work program." AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(J).

rows.title: Treatment program
rows.value: Participants in specified drug addiction or alcoholic treatment/rehabilitation programs are an excluded category.
rows.note: Use applicable program definitions; separate medical-frailty criteria may also matter.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Participants in a drug or alcohol rehabilitation or treatment program". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(K).

rows.title: Incarceration / recent release
rows.value: Inmates are specified excluded individuals; a mandatory exception addresses recent incarceration within the defined three-month look-back.
rows.note: DHCS public material describes release in the last 90 days; CMS uses a three-month period ending on the first day of the assessed month. Inmate exclusion does not promise routine Medicaid payment for all prison care.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: an exception for an inmate "at any point during the 3-month period ending on the first day of a month". DHCS: "People released from jail or prison in the last 90 days". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(L) and (f)(4).

rows.title: Medicare / other mandatory status
rows.value: For all or part of a reviewed month: Medicare Part A entitlement/enrollment, Part B enrollment, under age 19, specified other mandatory groups or excluded status can establish deemed compliance.
rows.note: This is distinct from claiming earned income. Actual eligibility category and review month must be established.
rows.evidence: CMS deck mandatory exceptions for all or part of a month. AB 2161 §14005.69(f)(1)–(5).

rows.title: Short-term hardship
rows.value: States may elect hardships for specified inpatient care, out-of-area serious-condition care, qualifying high-unemployment counties, or federal emergencies/disasters.
rows.note: DHCS outreach lists these circumstances. Do not assume a county qualifies: location, period, state adoption and notice must be checked.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet short-term hardship options. DHCS member letter: "If either one of these applies to your county, we will send you another notice." AB 2161 §14005.69(h)(1)–(4); the unemployment hardship is "subject to a request from the department to the United States Secretary".

sections.title: Coverage options & next steps
sections.description: A prioritized path to insurance or care, without assuming an income amount or county.
sections.intro: Research and publication were completed without requiring your input. Enrollment itself is not automated: official applications, documents and accurate household facts may be required. No insurance application was submitted and no personal account was accessed.

rows.title: 1 · Screen for Medi-Cal
rows.value: One Covered California application screens both programs; Medi-Cal applications are accepted year-round.
rows.note: If adult MAGI rules apply, check countable household income against the upper limit before assessing 2027 engagement. No earned-wage minimum is established for 2026 adult financial eligibility in these sources.
rows.evidence: How to Apply and program comparison; implementation starts in 2027.

rows.title: 2 · Income route first
rows.value: If countable MAGI-based monthly household income meets $580, the federal engagement income route may be available even without earned income.
rows.note: Recommended record set: income statements, rental income/expense records, tax records and trading statements. DHCS’s general list for self-employed applicants asks for Schedule C and a profit-and-loss statement for the last three months. This is practical preparation, not an assertion that the county requires or accepts exactly these documents for the work rule.
rows.evidence: Income methodology and available-data verification.

rows.title: 3 · If under threshold, choose a documented route
rows.value: Qualifying community service, training, work or education can satisfy the activity route; exclusions may make it unnecessary.
rows.note: Practical recommendation: structured nonprofit/public-organization service with dated verified hours is a clearer documented route than assuming own-account trading counts. No local placement is promised.
rows.evidence: Qualifying activities and outreach.

rows.title: 4 · Marketplace if financially ineligible
rows.value: Covered California offers private plans; financial help is income- and eligibility-dependent. Enrollment generally requires open enrollment or a qualifying special enrollment period.
rows.note: Expected annual MAGI includes relevant unearned income. For 2027, Covered California uses the previous year’s FPL, offers the state subsidy at 100%–200% FPL, and gives no federal premium tax credit above 400% FPL. Plan prices, subsidy eligibility and enrollment dates for this individual are blank/unverified; do not assume work-rule denial qualifies for subsidies.
rows.evidence: Covered California comparison; income guidance; subsidy warning.

rows.title: 5 · Other Medi-Cal pathways
rows.value: Non-MAGI and other coverage groups are outside the adult-expansion work rule described in California guidance.
rows.note: Ask for screening if age, disability, pregnancy, Medicare or another qualifying category applies. Property/income rules differ and asset limits may apply. This is not a workaround available solely because wages are zero.
rows.evidence: Excluded Populations and DHCS program comparison.

rows.title: 6 · Sliding-fee health center care
rows.value: HRSA health centers cannot deny services for inability to pay and use sliding-fee discounts; nominal charges may apply.
rows.note: Care access is not comprehensive insurance. Income and family size determine discounts; owning property does not establish a free visit. A specific provider or price was not verified.
rows.evidence: Chapter 9 Requirements.

rows.title: California administrative help
rows.value: DHCS says it may verify exemptions from existing information; BenefitsCal supports reporting, document upload and notices. The member letter describes investment in work/training/education resources.
rows.note: This is assistance implementing federal rules, not a verified blanket waiver for $0 earned income or a promise of no reporting. AB 2161 requires data-first verification, consent-based ways to add information, and confirmation of conflicting data before adverse action.
rows.evidence: What You Need to Do Now and corrected verification-first rule.

rows.title: Free enrollment support
rows.value: Covered California links free local enrollment help and lists (800) 300-1506. DHCS outreach lists Medi-Cal Helpline (800) 541-5555.
rows.note: Existing members: county office handles case questions and notices. Links in official pages lead to county contact directories; no county was assumed.
rows.evidence: Get Help / Questions.

rows.title: Respond and preserve appeal rights
rows.value: Keep contact details current, read notices and respond on time; adverse notices explain appeal rights.
rows.note: Recommendations: retain copies of submitted documents and notices; distinguish noncompliance denial from income denial when seeking review. AB 2161 requires the notice to state your right to a state hearing. No personal deadline is inferred.
rows.evidence: What You Need to Do Now; You Could Lose Your Medi-Cal; 30-day compliance notice.

sections.title: Flagged for Review
sections.description: Unresolved facts, contradictory official materials, and values deliberately left blank.
sections.intro: Blank confirmed-value cells are intentional. The evidence links establish the rule or conflict context; they do not verify the missing conclusion. These issues do not block publication, but they limit reliance on an individualized eligibility answer.

rows.title: Operative California dates
rows.note: CONFIRMED CONFLICT: S4 body says January 1, 2027, but its enclosed letter says both rules do not go into effect until March 2027 (and later says renewals beginning January). Current S5 says work January 1 and six-month checks March 1. The enacted statute (S19) says “no sooner than January 1, 2027”, only after DHCS confirms its systems are ready, and implementation waits for the director’s written systems determination (§14005.69(q)(1)). No official notice of that determination was located. Your operative application/renewal date is not assigned; do not assume a March work-rule delay.
rows.evidence: Read the S4 background and enclosure opening, plus S5 January/March sections. The inconsistency cannot be resolved from these texts alone.

rows.title: Kalshi tax classification and qualifying hours
rows.note: No official IRS or DHCS source reviewed established the treatment of this person’s specific Kalshi contracts, deductions, losses, timing or own-account activity hours. IRS Topic 429 is securities guidance, not a Kalshi ruling. Contract-specific §1256 eligibility and the personal MAGI amount remain blank.
rows.evidence: Official-targeted IRS Kalshi/event-contract searches (October 18 and October 19, 2026) produced no confirming official result. This is a research limitation, not proof no guidance exists.

rows.title: Property management qualifying hours
rows.note: The federal preamble says a property manager or building superintendent paid in free or reduced rent can count those hours, and that self-employment (owning a business) is work. No source reviewed resolves how your county will treat hours spent managing your own rentals versus services for clients, or which records it will accept. The corrected rule bars denial solely for documentation that does not exist (§435.557(b)(2)(iii)(B)). Neither 80 qualifying hours nor earned-income classification is assigned.
rows.evidence: 91 FR 33348 preamble II.C.1; 42 CFR 435.552(b); corrected §435.557(b)(2)(iii); DHCS self-employed documents list. General rules do not establish the person-specific conclusion.

rows.title: Actual eligibility, household and deadline
rows.note: Age, tax household, monthly/annual income, expenses, disability/caregiver status, county, current coverage/aid code and renewal month were not supplied. Eligibility, premium, subsidy, exemption and actual application look-back are unverified. No facts are inferred from a full-time trader/property-manager label.
rows.evidence: Official sources require eligibility facts and application/renewal review. No personal financial documents were provided.

rows.title: Annual ceilings: sizes 2, 5, 7, 10 and 12
rows.note: CONFIRMED CONFLICT: public DHCS S12 shows $29,863 / $53,378 / $69,055 / $92,570 / $108,247; annual enclosure S10 shows $29,864 / $53,379 / $69,056 / $92,571 / $108,248, rounded up. No single definitive annual value selected here. Monthly enclosures are distinct; do not resolve annual conflict by calculation.
rows.evidence: Both official 138% annual columns re-read in full on 2026-10-19; five one-dollar differences identified (sizes 2, 5, 7, 10 and 12).

rows.title: Public earnings wording versus federal income rule
rows.note: CONFIRMED WORDING DIFFERENCE: S5 activity bullets say work at a job and earn $580; S4 says income from any source; S3 and S20 use MAGI-based monthly household income, and the enacted state statute (S19 §14005.69(e)(6)) uses MAGI-based financial methods for the individual’s MAGI-based household budget. A wages-only interpretation is not supported by the federal rule or the statute. County treatment of your exact amounts is not assigned.
rows.evidence: Federal rule II.C.8 and CMS income slide directly address countable income; public shorthand is not a replacement for the rule.

rows.title: Seasonal averaging for fluctuating trading
rows.note: CONFIRMED CONFLICT: the S4 member letter (August 31, 2026) says people “whose hours change frequently or who have seasonal jobs” can average over six months. AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(7) (enacted September 14, 2026), 42 CFR 435.552(g)(1) and DHCS’s own S5 page limit averaging to seasonal workers. Under 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B) a seasonal worker is someone who “performs labor or services on a seasonal basis as defined by the Secretary of Labor”. No official source reviewed classifies own-account Kalshi trading as seasonal work. No six-month averaging entitlement assigned.
rows.evidence: Do not infer seasonal-worker status from variable investment returns.

rows.title: 2027 income ceilings and personal plan pricing
rows.note: Covered California’s 2027 chart (S22) says marketplace programs use the previous year’s FPL, and Medi-Cal uses the current year’s FPL as calculated by DHCS. A 2027 DHCS Medi-Cal chart and individualized plan quotes were not located. All published dollar ceilings here are 2026 reference figures. Future Medi-Cal limits, premiums and subsidies remain blank.
rows.evidence: S18 is explicitly a 2026 FPL letter; S22 shows 2026 DHCS Medi-Cal values “for reference”; Covered California directs applicants to its eligibility/application process.

rows.title: External link and full-document limits
rows.note: Every source in the register was re-fetched on 2026-10-19 (arena/75b1956e) and each row re-read against it; the source register records what was read. The build itself runs no automated external HTTP checks. The 135-page rule and full public law were not read end-to-end: rule text was checked through Federal Register full-text search and the codified eCFR section. This is a row-scoped verification, not a certification of every line of those documents.
rows.evidence: The source register distinguishes full retrieved text, search excerpts and cross-checks. Local site links are tested automatically.

rows.title: DHCS copayment income figure (October 2028)
rows.note: S5 says copayments from October 1, 2028 apply to adults 19–64 who “Make more than $15,560 a year”. DHCS’s own 2026 enclosure (S10) lists the one-person 100% FPL as 15960. The figures do not match, so no copayment threshold is stated here.
rows.evidence: Both DHCS pages re-read 2026-10-19; discrepancy reported, not resolved.

rows.title: School wording: part time versus half-time
rows.note: CONFIRMED WORDING DIFFERENCE: the S4 member letter says “Go to school at least part time”. AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(4), 42 CFR 435.552(a)(4) and DHCS’s S5 page require enrollment at least half-time; less-than-half-time hours count only when combined with other activities. No lower standard is assigned here.
rows.evidence: S5: “Go to school at least half-time (usually two or three classes, or about six to eight credits each semester)”.
